It's worth noting that the most prominent person associated with the name "McCoy" in the design world is **Katherine McCoy** (sometimes referred to as Catherine McCoy). Here is a detailed overview:

---

## Katherine (Catherine) McCoy

Katherine McCoy (born October 12, 1945) is an American graphic designer and educator, best known for her work as the co-chair of the graduate Design program for Cranbrook Academy of Art.

### Early Life & Education
McCoy was born Katherine Jane Braden in Decatur, Illinois in 1945. As a student, she first studied interior design at Michigan State University but switched to industrial design, in which field she graduated in 1967.

### Career
Shortly after graduation, McCoy joined Unimark International, a design firm led by many key figures in American Modernist graphic design, including Massimo Vignelli and Herbert Bayer. It was at Unimark where McCoy was exposed to strict Swiss typographic and design approaches which came to permeate much of American corporate communications through the late 1960s and 70s.

Following Unimark, McCoy worked for a year in the corporate identity offices of the Chrysler Corporation, then joined the Boston design firm Omnigraphics, where she worked on several projects for the MIT Press with Muriel Cooper.

In 1971 she founded the practice McCoy & McCoy, Inc. with her husband, Michael McCoy. That same year, she began her career in design education when she was appointed co-chair of the Cranbrook Academy of Art graduate design program.

### Cranbrook Academy of Art
In 1971, McCoy became co-chair, with her husband Mike McCoy, of the design department at Cranbrook Academy of Art, which they continued to direct until 1995. By the 1980s, their sometimes controversial programme had established itself as one of the most innovative in American design education, producing a stream of graduates who have gone on to make their own mark in the profession.

Katherine and Michael McCoy revised the design program at Cranbrook Academy of Art: instead of deadlines and conventional exams, they offered experimentation, self-evaluation, and weekly critiques.

### Teaching Philosophy
After coming to Cranbrook, she experimented with various expressive means to communicate through graphic design other than Swiss style or Modernism, which she found rather limiting. She openly rejected their sterile approach and encouraged her students to conduct design experiments that expanded design vocabulary.

### Honors & Leadership
During her tenure as co-chair of Cranbrook, she was on the board of editors for *Industrial Design Magazine* and was the executive vice president of the Industrial Designers Society of America (IDSA). She was also a member of Alliance Graphique Internationale and the president of the American Center of Design. In 1983, she was elected to a 2-year term as the president of the IDSA — not only the first woman but the youngest person to do so.

In 1994, the McCoys were jointly awarded a Chrysler Award for Innovation in Design.

### Later Work
McCoy's career in education was broadly expansive, teaching at Cranbrook Academy of Art, Illinois Institute of Technology's Institute of Design, and the Royal College of Art, London.

Since 1997, she and Michael have hosted the High Ground Design Conversation, an annual gathering of design curators, critics, and educators.

McCoy continues her graphic design practice, with most of her work being civic-minded, focused on spreading the mission of design for a better world.

---

In summary, Katherine McCoy is a towering figure in American graphic design and design education, celebrated for transforming design thinking through her innovative and experimental approach at Cranbrook Academy of Art.
